On 29 May 2026, ahead of World No Tobacco Day on 31 May, the World Health Organization (WHO) urged governments to protect young people from addiction to tobacco and nicotine products.
The WHO says at least 40 million children aged 13 to 15 use tobacco products, and that young people's use of e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches continues to rise.
It says tobacco and nicotine companies are deliberately engineering products to be more appealing, easier to use and harder to quit, especially for adolescents.
The WHO calls on governments to ban flavoured products, ban advertising, promotion and sponsorship, make indoor public places completely smoke- and vape-free, and step up enforcement.
